      "claim_sha256": "fb9ae60f99faf3eb5965587e290b6f09ce1b6a2e216a09df2acdac8e0de8d119",
      "evidence": "Let (M,Q) witness that H=G[N(v)] is WKE. The triangles S={vxy:xy∈M} are edge-disjoint because M is a matching. For X=M∪{vq:q∈Q}, |X|=|M|+|Q|≤2|S|. Every triangle through v is hit by X: its link edge is either in M or, being in H−M, has an endpoint in Q. With G'=(G−X)−v, S is edge-disjoint from every packing in G' because its non-v edges lie in M⊆X. Thus ν(G)≥|M|+ν(G'), while X united with a transversal of G' gives τ(G)≤|X|+τ(G').       "search_method": "Direct definition-level proof with the empty-matching and residual cases included",

    },

      "claim": "Every graph whose every nonempty subgraph has a vertex with WKE link satisfies τ≤2ν.",

      "evidence": "Induct on the number of vertices. Apply claim 0 at a guaranteed vertex v. The residual G' is a proper subgraph. Every nonempty subgraph of G' is also a subgraph of G, and the hypothesis concerns links inside each such subgraph, so the hypothesis is inherited without a quantifier change. Induction proves the inequality for G', and the WKE reduction transfers it to G.",
      "idx": 1,
      "search_method": "Inductive proof with explicit hereditary-quantifier audit",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"
    },
    {
      "checker_path": "none",
      "claim": "Every locally bipartite graph satisfies τ≤2ν.",
      "claim_sha256": "4d19cc68d4f144e891cd4ad6582415d1e6d44282e7eab072c0667320437ac61f",
      "evidence": "For every subgraph J⊆G and v∈V(J), J[N_J(v)] is a subgraph of the bipartite graph G[N_G(v)], hence is bipartite. By König's theorem, a bipartite link has a matching M and vertex cover Q with |Q|=|M|, which is a WKE witness since Q also covers the link after M is deleted. Thus every nonempty subgraph has a vertex with WKE link, and claim 1 applies.",
      "idx": 2,
      "search_method": "Hereditary link analysis followed by the matching-cover equality for bipartite graphs",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"
    },
    {
      "checker_path": "<workspace-home>/paired_hard_v1_scratch/hard_tuza_triangle_packing_covering/audit-revision/bugbank/iter_1/check_wke_threshold.py",
      "claim": "Every triangle-free graph on at most eight vertices is WKE.",

      "evidence": "The checker generated labelled triangle-free graphs recursively: a new labelled vertex was joined to each independent subset of the existing graph. This is exhaustive and duplication-free because deleting the newest vertex gives the unique parent, and its neighborhood is independent exactly when no new triangle is formed. For each Q, the complete WKE test used the equivalence that all edges induced by R=V−Q must form a matching forced into M and must extend to a matching of size at least |Q|; every returned (M,Q) was then checked literally against the WKE definition. Counts of generated graphs and validated witnesses agreed at every order 0–8, culminating in 4,682,270 of each at order eight. The checker exited with PASS using integer bit masks only.",
      "idx": 3,
      "search_method": "Exact exhaustive labelled-graph generation and complete matching/cover enumeration",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "A literal WKE pair (M,Q) was constructed and validated for every one of the 4,682,270 labelled order-eight triangle-free graphs and for every generated smaller graph."

    {
      "checker_path": "<workspace-home>/paired_hard_v1_scratch/hard_tuza_triangle_packing_covering/audit-revision/bugbank/iter_1/check_wke_threshold.py",
      "claim": "The order-eight WKE bound is sharp: a triangle-free non-WKE graph exists on nine vertices.",
      "claim_sha256": "50aa7622da183bbdd438881436bf7ba269e1139ce509a67caae9bb3df3356e78",
      "evidence": "Take independent cyclic parts A0={0}, A1={1,2}, A2={3,4}, A3={5,6}, A4={7,8}, with all edges between consecutive parts. This graph is triangle-free. Any vertex subset inducing maximum degree at most one has order at most four: if it contains both vertices of a two-vertex part, both adjacent parts must be empty and the remaining two parts contribute at most two; if it contains at most one vertex per part, selecting five induces C5. In any WKE witness, |M|≤4 and hence R=V−Q has at least five vertices, while every edge of H[R] must lie in M, forcing H[R] to have maximum degree at most one—a contradiction. Independently, the checker found the maximum such R has order four and rejected all 33,701 eligible (M,Q) pairs across all 275 matchings.",

      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"

      "claim": "Triangle packing and covering are additive over triangle edge-overlap components.",

      "evidence": "Distinct edge-overlap classes have disjoint edge supports; otherwise triangles containing a common support edge would lie in the same class. Packings from the classes can therefore be united without an edge conflict, and every global packing restricts to packings in the classes, proving ν=Σν_i. Likewise, unions of component transversals cover all triangles, while every global transversal restricts to a transversal of each class; disjoint support edge sets give τ=Στ_i. Claim 6 then sums the component inequalities, and claim 5 disposes of all edges outside the triangle supports.",

          "body_md": "## Object\n\nDefine $x \\sim y \\iff x - y \\in \\mathbb{Q}$; pick $V \\subset [0,1]$ meeting each\nequivalence class once. Measurability is a\ngenuine hypothesis on every set appearing in a measure-theoretic argument — including\nsets produced *inside* proofs by choice, projections, or images (cf. the Cantor-function\nhomeomorphism trick producing nonmeasurable images of measurable sets).\n\n## Debugging uses\n\n- Immediate check on any construction that defines a set via unrestricted choice or\n  via an uncountable union and then integrates over it.\n- Explains the architecture of probability theory: σ-algebras exist because of V.\n  \"Pick a uniform random real and ask P(X ∈ V)\" is undefined — a useful reminder that\n  event spaces in modeling are a modeling decision, not bookkeeping.\n- Choice-sensitivity lint (cf. hamel-additive-function): in Solovay's model all sets\n  are measurable, so any claimed *explicit* (choice-free, Borel) nonmeasurable set is\n  wrong — Borel sets are always measurable.\n\n## Remarks\n\nBanach–Tarski is the 3D escalation (finite additivity also fails there); in dimensions\n1 and 2 finitely additive invariant extensions to all subsets do exist (Banach), so\ncountable additivity is exactly what V breaks.",
